profile.reading:
Per Flexential's own individual facility page, this building (Flexential Las Vegas - North) is located at 3330 East Lone Mountain Road, North Las Vegas, NV 89081. The operator publishes a footprint of 111240 square feet and 9 MW of critical load UPS capacity for this specific building, with published certifications and compliance attestations including PCI DSS, SOC 1 Type II, SOC 2 Type II, SOC 3, HITRUST, NIST 800-53, ITAR, SSAE 18. Nevada launched its data center sales- and property-tax abatement program in 2015 as a post-recession economic development tool; a Nevada Independent analysis found the state had approved $457 million in combined projected tax abatements over the following decade (15 abatements, 2 later withdrawn) and that local governments missed out on more than $537 million in sales and use tax revenue over eight years, while the abated projects promised roughly 300 permanent jobs, or about $1.5 million in incentive per job, far above the roughly $190,000 per job Nevada offered Tesla for 6,500 positions. A 2023 analysis found Nevada's data center sector overall, including non-abated facilities, employed 4,550 people and generated $290 million in state and local tax revenue. Storey County, east of Reno, hosts more than half of the state's abated data centers, including Google and Switch facilities, a different submarket from Flexential's Las Vegas-area buildings. Union electrical workers reported heavy construction activity tied to data centers, with one Northern Nevada local reporting 4,000 electricians deployed, about 80% on data center projects.

Clark County, home to both Las Vegas Flexential buildings, is a distinct jurisdiction from the Storey County tax-abatement submarket near Reno and has its own active 2026 data center policy debate. Switch operates 11 data centers spanning more than 2 million square feet in the Las Vegas area; Clark County commissioners approved a roughly 57,000-square-foot expansion of an existing Switch facility in southwest Las Vegas on June 17, 2026, after opposition from Sierra Club members and area residents, and on July 7, 2026 directed staff to study new land-use and environmental standards for data centers amid growing calls for regulation, according to the Nevada Independent and Las Vegas Review-Journal. Separately, Google's Henderson data center consumed more than 404 million gallons of water for cooling in 2024, non-recoverable water converted to mist, even after the Southern Nevada Water Authority banned evaporative cooling in new commercial buildings in 2023 (Google's facility was grandfathered in); data centers accounted for about 22% of Nevada's electricity consumption in 2024, with NV Energy projecting statewide data center load could reach 64% of the utility's electricity sales by 2046, per FOX5 Las Vegas investigative reporting.

reading.body:
Flexential Las Vegas - North publishes 9 MW of IT capacity across 111,000 square feet, enough to support roughly 225 GPU-dense racks or 900 traditional colocation racks depending on actual customer workload density.

The certification stack qualifies this campus for heavily regulated AI workloads. SOC 1 Type II and SOC 2 Type II cover financial and operational controls. PCI DSS qualifies it for payment card data. ITAR qualifies it for export-controlled defense technical data. NIST 800-53 aligns it with federal security controls. HITRUST qualifies it for healthcare information. These certifications open the facility to finance, defense, and healthcare tenants, though which ones occupy it is unpublished.

Within Nevada, this campus ranks first by published IT capacity. This ranking reflects a data gap rather than dominance. Only one of 26 mapped facilities in the state has published a power figure on its operator spec page. The remaining 25 publish no megawatt capacity, so the 9 MW total for Nevada here represents only what operators have chosen to disclose, not the true installed base.
